主要内容: Fidelity Investments reported a record profit and revenue in 2018, despite a challenging market environment. The Boston-based asset manager saw its operating income rise by 19 percent, while revenue increased by 12 percent to a record $20.4 billion. For the first time in history, Fidelity's annual income exceeded $6 billion. The firm's success was attributed to its long-term diversification efforts, expanding beyond traditional stock-picking into areas like retail brokerage, workplace benefits, and institutional investing. Despite a decline in assets under administration by 1.5 percent, Fidelity's mutual funds outperformed peers by 66 percent, 72 percent, and 76 percent for the trailing one, three, and five-year periods, respectively. The company also launched zero-fee funds, which attracted $2.9 billion in assets from clients. Fidelity's customer base grew to 31.1 million workplace and health care participants in 2018, a 6 percent increase from the previous year. Fidelity, a family-controlled firm, reported record profit and revenue, with retail clients increasing by 7% year-over-year. The company's clearing and custody platform managed 7.1 million accounts, up 6.5% from year-end 2017. Fidelity is known for managing retirement plans and mutual funds, but it also invests heavily in technology, spending around $2.5 billion annually on blockchain and artificial intelligence through Fidelity Labs and its Fidelity Center for Applied Technology. In October, Fidelity launched a new company, Fidelity Digital Asset Services, to offer custody services for cryptocurrencies. The new company implemented its first institutional client in December, as stated in the shareholder letter.
